1
Setup

Product Groups & Creative Focus Group

▸
Upload all dropdown lists from a file

Fastest way to fill in the lists below. Upload a .csv or .xlsx laid out the same way as a typical Lookups tab: one column per list (Product Group, Creative Focus Group, Audience, Buy Type, Media Type, Partner), the list's values going down that column. Any other columns (Marketing Group/Channel, Impressions, Project Number, etc.) are recognized and skipped automatically — Marketing Group uses a fixed, shared list, and Impressions/Project Number aren't dropdown lists at all. 2
Onboarding

Create campaigns from a file

▸

For getting a client up and running fast — not for everyday use. Rows that share a Project Number become one campaign (its sends, drops or insertions are the line items; the campaign runs from the earliest hit date to the latest end date). Rows without one are grouped by Channel + Partner + Hit Date + End Date + Audience — not by name, since clients don't always have one. campaignName is just a display label. A row whose match already exists on this account adds its line item to that campaign's Channel Planning Detail — existing rows are kept, not replaced — so re-uploading a corrected file is always safe. A combination Verilume hasn't seen before is created as a new campaign with its own campaign ID.

Date range for this file
Describes what this file covers, for the upload history below — not a hard boundary on the dates inside individual rows.
Get the template
One header row, one example row. Rows are grouped/matched by channel + partner + hitDate + endDate + audience — campaignName is a display label only, not part of the match. A row can carry several Product Groups or Creative Focus Groups — separate them with commas (Polar, Epicurean). Your own column names are fine too (Marketing Group, Partner, Budget, Drop/Hit/End Date, Size, Specs, 1st Proof Due, Creative Due, QR Code Link, Phone, Notes, Project Number…) — they're matched on upload, and dollar signs, thousands separators and m/d/yyyy dates are read as-is. On Magazines and Newspapers rows, Partner + Size registers the ad format in your print-spec catalog and seeds its cost per insertion from Budget where none is saved yet. Production columns (List Request, List Due, Release Files, In Home, Format, Total/Mail Qty, Paper & Manufacturing, Postage/Freight, Insertion, Cost, Unit Cost, Vendor…) are captured on each line item and editable afterwards under Marketing Ops → Production Schedule & Details.
The second download carries every line item with its Verilume campaign id and line id — edit it and upload it back here to update in place.

Voice

✓

1
Keywords

Brand & product keyword chips

▸

Phrases you always say a particular way, like a program name or a signature line. Unlike the keywords above, these are copied exactly, with this spelling and capitalisation. Every copy prompt receives them, and a draft that leaves one out or rewords it loses Brand Fit points.

Always include: every draft must contain it. Use when it fits: use it where it belongs, never reworded. Protect wording: if the copy mentions it, spelling and capitalisation stay exact.
2
Negative keywords

Terms to avoid

▸

Enter words or short phrases that are not consistent with your product mission and positioning — specific terms to exclude (e.g. "cheap," "hack") as well as tones or styles to avoid sounding like (e.g. "budget airline chipper," "corporate jargon").

This list drives real exclusions, not just a record: it's kept out of the generated Voice draft and the Brand & Product Keywords above, and it's what campaign copy is checked against for the Brand Voice guardrail/compliance flag shown in campaign briefs and the Daily Brief. Add a short tone/style phrase (not just single words) to also steer the Voice draft's "what this voice is not" framing.
3
Positive keywords

Terms to emphasize

▸

Enter words or short phrases this brand actively wants to sound like — specific terms to lean into (e.g. "restraint," "specificity") as well as tones or registers to reach for (e.g. "poetic precision, not promotional excitement").

Same treatment as Terms to Avoid, in the opposite direction: a short term shows up as its own "emphasize" line in the generated Voice Guide, and a longer tone/register phrase gets woven into a Tone Rule. Both are also always shown in a short guidance line at the end of the guide, so this can't quietly disappear on a future draft.

Draws on everything above — Brand Keywords, Terms to avoid, and Terms to emphasize — plus your real Products & Services and Sample Writings, to draft the full Voice Guide below with an actual AI call.

Colors & Fonts

Optional
The actual logo file, so it can appear in the portal header. SVG (preferred, scales cleanly) or transparent PNG/WebP — no JPG. Long side roughly 400-1200px. Optional

Optional
Which colors are backgrounds vs. accents vs. rare, and what to avoid — stops a generated brief from treating every listed color as equally usable everywhere.
What makes this brand's headlines recognizable — italic, all-caps, tight tracking — since a brief can't infer it from the font name alone.
Legibility rules more than personality here — anything that keeps long-form copy readable at small sizes.
Optional

Optional
Photography direction, creative principles, do's/don'ts — the field with the most leverage on this page. A blank field means every brief defaults to generic guidance.

    Brand Groundwork · Brand Book · Sample Writings & Presentations

    Sample Writings & Presentations

    Reference library of real writing and presentation samples for this brand — always categorized by purpose and date, so every Campaign/Project can pull the right precedent instead of guessing which file is current. Files (Word, PDF, PowerPoint) route through the same PII/virus-scan pipeline as Market Optimization and Marketing Budget Upload before they're stored. Google Docs and Google Slides aren't files this prototype can fetch, so those go in as a labeled reference link instead. A short video (up to :30 seconds) can also be analyzed for visual style and on-screen text — see Option C below; the video itself is never stored, only the written analysis. Any sample can also be scoped to one Product Group (e.g. Antarctica) instead of the whole account — that's what feeds AI copy generation genuine, destination-specific detail (named excursions, onboard programs, culinary depth) instead of generic language; see Option D below for reading a document straight from a published URL when it's too large to upload.

    Option A

    Upload a file

    ▸

    Accepts Word (.doc, .docx), PDF (.pdf), and PowerPoint (.ppt, .pptx). Every file is screened for PII and scanned for threats before it's stored — same pipeline as the other upload features in this build, never the filename-only path.

    Scope this sample to one product group and it feeds ONLY that group's AI copy generation.

    Scope this sample to one destination or ship (e.g. Antarctica, Mediterranean) and it feeds ONLY that destination's AI copy and video-script generation as Internal Experience Evidence — named excursions, onboard programs, culinary detail, anything that makes copy read as genuinely specific rather than generic.         CMO Dashboard / Media Plan
        Media Plan

        Annual Media Plan

        Built from what the brand needs on an ongoing basis — not a response to any one campaign. Allocates the annual budget across the Media Loop stages, then across channels within each stage, with a recommended starting split you can adjust anywhere. Campaigns can draw against these allocations, or run Unplanned, outside the plan entirely — see cxmedia-media-plan-budget-scope.md for the full design.

        Budget setup

        One place to set up and manage each year's marketing budget — upload the file you already have, build it by hand from a total or a revenue target, or start from a previous year.

        Start here

        Plan Setup

        🗓

        Pick a budget scope and year. If a budget already exists for it you'll see it marked Active below; if not, choose how to set it up — Upload, Manually add, or Leverage a previous year.

        Each plan line gets its Marketing Loop stage from its channel and audience. Past Customers spend is Loyalty. Brand Search and Remarketing (anonymous visitors) are Purchase. Hand-Raisers are Consideration. New to Brand (Prospects) is Awareness unless the line targets a brand or product group, then Consideration. PR, Partner Media and anything marked Advocacy are Advocacy. A stage you set by hand on a line is kept.

        Setup — Upload

        Upload your budget file

        📤

        Accepts .csv or .xlsx, any layout — standard flat table or a multi-section export like a real annual budget workbook.

        ✦
        This looks for month names (Jan–Dec) across every row to find your file's header(s) — if it finds exactly one, that's a standard flat table. If it finds several (a client export that repeats a header block per category, like a real Print/Direct Mail/Digital/Trade section layout), that's reported as a multi-block file: month and total columns still auto-recognize from their own header text, but the category-name and Working/Non-Working columns usually aren't labeled clearly enough to guess, so you confirm those. It also checks the math — if one row's total equals the sum of the others in its block, that's very likely a subtotal, not its own line item, and gets flagged so it isn't double-counted (or silently dropped).
        ⬇ Download sample template

        Not sure how to format your file? Download the template — it shows the column layout we recognize automatically (Category, Working/Non-Working, one column per month, Total).

        Annual plan — baseline & targets

        🎯

        The year's full-funnel numbers, in the annual model's own vocabulary: Baseline is the trailing-12-month actuals the plan was calibrated on; Target is the approved scenario for the year. Campaign Summaries model each campaign off the Baseline's rates (cost per website user, value-lead and growth-lead rates, impressions → bookings) and show every campaign metric as a share of the Target.         Manual bridge — until CRM / form integrations

        Leads by type, by month

        📇

        Source (website, Meta, coreg, transaction…) × Lead Type (High Value, Growth or Prospect) × Form Name, count of emails, per month — plus, when you have them, Bookings and Avg Days to Convert per row (upload columns: Month, Source, Lead Type, Form Name, Total Leads, Bookings, Avg Days to Convert; Conversion Rate is derived, not stored). Three lead types: High Value = the annual model's value leads (talk to expert / quote / request info); Growth (stored as Registration) = subscribe / brochure / popup / share / contact; Prospect = Meta lead forms and co-registration. Measured per-pool conversion and days-to-convert override the stage seeds in the campaign funnel, Transaction Window and timing.

        SourceLead typeForm nameCount of emailBookingsAvg days to convert

        Manual bridge — until the booking / order integration

        Unique transactions by month, by Product Group

        🧾

        Unique transactions (and revenue, if you have it) per month per Product Group — use the account's Marketing Calendar Product Groups so campaigns tagged with a Product Group read their own actuals; leave Product Group blank for an all-products row. Upload a file with a Month column to load a whole year at once.

        Customer-level file = one row per customer (or per line): Transaction Date, Transaction / Order Code, Transaction Type, Promo Type, Status, Service or Delivery Date, Age, Customer State / Postal Code / Country, Gross Revenue, Net Revenue, Product Group, Creative Focus — any subset, any column names close to those. Unique transactions = distinct transaction codes per month (two customers on one code count once); customers and revenue are kept per row. Which status values count and how each transaction type maps to a class and to marketing-attributable are this account's own settings (below, seeded from your data with generic suggestions). Whole periods in the file are replaced, so one multi-year file is fine and can be re-uploaded.

        Product GroupUnique transactionsRevenue (optional)

        GA4 → Explore → Free form: Year, Week, Session campaign, Session source / medium, Event name, Sessions, Engaged sessions, Key events. Upload the .csv as it comes. We keep sessions, engaged sessions and key events by week, campaign and source, and key events by name (calls, popups, forms). GA4 stops a free-form export at 100,000 rows, so for a long range export it in shorter date ranges or filter to key events.
